supported_claims.text: The graph’s construction is unsettled. A historical account interprets it as one act yielding two; other proposals read its ancient form as fish-related or as a cord-making tool. These remain competing explanations, not a confirmed component analysis.

Bronze inscriptions use 再 for “again/second time” and for “two”; Warring States bamboo texts include 再三. The cited sources do not establish absolute dates for these examples or which attested use came first.

A Guodian slip may use the whole graph 再 to write 在. If so, this is a proposed borrowing of the sign for a different word, not evidence that 再’s meaning developed into 在; the interpretation is uncertain.

The supplied evidence supports no phonetic-component analysis for 再. The checked readings of 冓 and 再 differ in Mandarin and in the supplied Baxter–Sagart Middle and Old Chinese data, but these readings alone do not settle the graph’s construction.
The curated seal-style image is a modern vector redraw representing a later script style; it is not an ancient artifact image and does not establish a sequence of graphic development.

disagreements.text: The fish proposal interprets 冓 as two fish meeting, while the cord-tool proposal treats the graph as a weaving implement. The historical account that reads the graph as 一 with abbreviated 冓, expressing one act yielding two, is another distinct explanation. The dossier does not resolve these analyses.

The role of 二 in some Warring States forms is uncertain: it may contribute the meaning “two,” but those forms may also include it decoratively. This does not establish 二 as a component of the graph in every form.

limitations.text: The earliest documented corpus use and original referent of 再 are not established by the supplied evidence. Fragmentary oracle-bone contexts and reported bronze uses do not establish a direct semantic or graphic transition between them.
The evidence does not provide a complete dated sequence from ancient forms to the modern standard shape, nor does it support a claim of graphic corruption.
Although readings for 冓 and 再 are supplied, they do not independently establish 冓’s identity or a sound role within 再. The local reading rows are not externally verified in this dossier.
The dossier’s “two fish caught on a line” gloss is too definite for the reported evidence: the fish interpretation remains uncertain, and the cited account says the graph differs from 魚.
